name: Dacz Golf
description: Dacz Golf is a high-interaction variant of the classic Golf card game, belonging to the 'Power Card' family (including Cabo and Cambio). Unlike standard Golf, players can use 'Power Cards' drawn from the deck to peek at cards, swap with opponents, or manipulate the layout. The goal remains to have the lowest scoring layout, but the addition of hidden information and unexpected swaps makes it a game of memory, bluffing, and tactical timing. It is known as 'Dacz' in Poland and 'Power Golf' elsewhere.

content.text: Dacz Golf is a high-interaction variant of the classic Golf card game, belonging to the 'Power Card' family (including Cabo and Cambio). Unlike standard Golf, players can use 'Power Cards' drawn from the deck to peek at cards, swap with opponents, or manipulate the layout. The goal remains to have the lowest scoring layout, but the addition of hidden information and unexpected swaps makes it a game of memory, bluffing, and tactical timing. It is known as 'Dacz' in Poland and 'Power Golf' elsewhere.

Derived from the traditional game of Golf, the 'Power' variants emerged in the late 20th century. Names like 'Cambio' (Spain) and 'Cabo' suggest a global spread through traveler communities and local evolution.

Two to six players; the game is often best with two to four. Four-card Golf and its power-card variants (Dacz, Cabo, Cambio, Cactus) can in theory be played by two to around eight or more; with eight or more players, two packs are shuffled together. Commercial and folk accounts typically describe play with 2-6 players.

Each player is dealt 4 cards face-down in a row. Before play begins, each player may peek at their two outer cards (or two inner, by agreement). The rest of the deck forms the stock; one card is turned up to start the discard pile.

items.text: Cabo (Commercial): Uses specific rhymes: 7/8 (Know your fate - peek own), 9/10 (Know a friend - peek opponent), J/Q (Switch between). King of Diamonds is 0, others 13.
Cambio (Spanish): Often played with Jokers (-5). More aggressive swapping rules.
Cactus (Vancouver): Queens swap any card. 9/10/J peek opponent. 6/7/8 peek own. Call 'Cactus' to end.
